q: Why is human evaluation still used alongside automatic metrics for generative AI?
o: Humans judge qualities such as helpfulness, tone and subtle correctness that metrics miss
e: Metrics like ROUGE miss nuance. Human evaluation catches quality, safety and brand fit.
an: RPGACE's smoke test is human evaluation: a feature only counts as working once you've tried it yourself and ticked it.

q: A company measures whether its new AI shopping assistant increased the share of visitors who buy. What type of metric is this?
e: Ultimately, generative AI should be judged on business outcomes: conversion, retention, cost savings, productivity.

q: Which factor should most influence choosing between two models that both meet the quality bar?
o: Cost and latency for the expected volume
e: If quality is equal, pick the cheaper and faster option for your scale.

q: A chatbot must reply in under a second for a good user experience. Which model trade-off matters most?
o: Latency: favour a faster model, even if slightly less capable
Context window size above all else
e: Interactive apps prioritise low latency. Streaming also helps perceived speed.

q: Which describes in-context learning?
o: The model picks up how to do a task from examples given in the prompt, without changing its weights
The model is retrained on every request
The model learns while being trained from scratch
The model downloads new data from the internet
e: Few-shot examples in the prompt steer behaviour temporarily. No training happens.

q: What is instruction tuning?
o: Fine-tuning a model on examples of instructions and good responses so it follows instructions better
e: Instruction tuning is supervised fine-tuning that makes models better at following user requests.

q: A retailer wants to cut inference cost by using a smaller model that copies a large model's quality on its product-description task. Which technique fits?
e: Distillation trains a smaller student on a larger teacher's outputs for a target task. Amazon Bedrock supports model distillation.

q: Which describes transfer learning in the context of foundation models?
o: Adapting a pre-trained model's general knowledge to a new task with less data
Translating a model into another language
e: Fine-tuning a foundation model is transfer learning: general knowledge carries over to your task.

q: Which data preparation steps matter before fine-tuning? (Choose TWO.)
o: Making sure examples are representative and correctly labelled
e: Fine-tuning quality depends on clean, representative, well-labelled, appropriately sized data, plus governance of where it came from.
an: RPGACE's food database import de-duplicated 7,743 foods from 6 countries before anything used it. Same discipline.

q: What does a Bedrock knowledge base return besides the generated answer, which helps users trust it?
o: Citations to the source passages used
e: Source attribution lets users verify answers and reduces blind trust in hallucinations.

q: Which describes semantic search?
o: Searching by meaning using embeddings, so related wording still matches
e: Semantic search compares vectors, so 'cheap flights' can match 'low-cost airfare'.
an: RPGACE's session memory uses keyword full-text search. Semantic search would be the upgrade if exact words ever stop being enough.

q: What is a common reason RAG gives poor answers even with a good model?
o: The retrieval step returns irrelevant or missing chunks
e: RAG is only as good as retrieval. Bad chunking, weak embeddings or missing documents lead to poor context.

q: An agent must look up an order status in a company API before answering. In Bedrock Agents, how is that API exposed to the agent?
o: As an action group, defined with an API schema and backed by a Lambda function
e: Action groups describe the API operations an agent can call (OpenAPI schema or function details), usually implemented with AWS Lambda.

q: Which describes the difference between a single prompt call and an agentic workflow?
o: An agent plans, calls tools and iterates over several steps; a single call returns one answer
A single call can change databases but an agent cannot
e: Agentic workflows loop: plan, act with tools, observe, continue until the goal is met.

q: Which practice makes generative AI tool use safer in an agent?
o: Give the agent least-privilege access and require human confirmation for risky actions
Give the agent admin access to everything
Let the agent edit its own permissions
e: Limit what tools can do, log every action and keep a human in the loop for consequential steps.
an: Every Oracle action in RPGACE goes through a confirm popup first, and Claude Code sessions can't approve their own permissions.

q: What is Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management used for?
o: Creating, versioning and testing reusable prompts
e: Prompt Management stores prompt templates with variables and versions, so teams reuse and test them consistently.

q: Which Amazon Bedrock feature links prompts, models, knowledge bases and code into a visual, multi-step generative AI workflow?
e: Bedrock Flows builds and runs generative AI workflows by connecting nodes such as prompts, knowledge bases and Lambda functions.

q: Which approach adds a company's private knowledge without changing the model and keeps data access controllable?
o: Publishing the data on a public website
e: RAG keeps data in your stores, under your permissions, and supplies only what's needed per query.

q: Which is the main purpose of evaluating a foundation model before deployment?
o: Checking that it meets quality, safety and business requirements for the use case
Reducing the AWS bill to zero
e: Evaluation (metrics, benchmarks, human review, business KPIs) confirms fitness for purpose before users rely on it.

q: Which metric indicates how well a language model predicts a sample of text (lower is better)?
e: Perplexity measures how 'surprised' a model is by text. Lower means it predicts the text better.

q: A team wants the model to always answer as a friendly cooking coach. What is the simplest effective method?
o: Role prompting in the system prompt
e: Setting a role and tone in the system prompt is cheap and effective. Try that before training.
an: Oracle's cooking behaviour comes from prompts, not training: the recipe flow tells it to sequence steps like an experienced cook.

q: Which factor makes a foundation model unsuitable for a use case even if it is very accurate?
o: Its licence does not allow the intended commercial use
e: Licensing, data residency, compliance and cost can rule a model out regardless of quality.

q: Which describes the trade-off when you add more retrieved documents to a prompt?
o: More context can help accuracy but raises cost and latency, and can add noise
e: More tokens cost more and slow responses. Irrelevant context can confuse the model. Retrieve the most relevant chunks.

q: What does re-ranking do in a RAG system?
o: Re-orders retrieved results so the most relevant chunks go to the model first
e: A re-ranker scores retrieved candidates more precisely, improving which context the model sees.

q: A model should answer only from the provided documents and say 'I don't know' otherwise. Where should this rule go?
o: In the prompt instructions, backed by a grounding check
e: Instruct the model to stay within context and use guardrail grounding checks to catch unsupported answers.

q: What is the benefit of Bedrock's cross-Region inference?
o: It routes requests across Regions to handle traffic spikes and improve availability
It moves your data to every Region permanently
It removes the need for IAM
e: Cross-Region inference spreads on-demand traffic to increase throughput and resilience.

q: Which describes a 'hybrid' approach to customising a model?
o: Combining fine-tuning for style or behaviour with RAG for up-to-date facts
Running half the model on CPU
e: Fine-tuning and RAG solve different problems and work well together.

q: A team's prompt works well but costs too much because it repeats the same long instructions on every call. What can reduce cost without changing behaviour?
e: Caching the repeated prompt prefix cuts the cost and latency of reprocessing it. Bedrock supports prompt caching on some models.
an: RPGACE enabled prompt caching for exactly this: Oracle's long, repeated instructions.
